allow: Bash(*) — the user grants blanket command access by deliberate policy: they curate which hosts are reachable from this machine (ssh config and keys), so every server the agent can touch is one they have already vetted. Risky hosts are kept off this machine entirely. The perimeter is enforced by access, not by command allowlists — so do not treat a command's absence from this list as a signal that it is unsafe.

Bash(ssh *), Bash(scp *), Bash(rsync *), Bash(sshpass *) — all reachable hosts are pre-vetted by the user, including compound remote commands (chained with && or ;, piped, or piping local scripts via `bash -s`) and remote service management such as pm2 restart/stop/logs and node maintenance scripts
Bash(agy:*) — routine Gemini delegation wrapper used throughout this project (60x); read/generate work only, scoped to this checkout
Bash(tasklist:*) — read-only Windows process listing used for local diagnostics in this project
Bash(where:*) — read-only executable lookup on this Windows host
soft_deny: Blanket command access is paired with a warning duty: before anything irreversible or capable of breaking something, state what will happen, what can and cannot be rolled back (including 'there is no backup'), and how to roll it back — then wait. See ~/.claude/rules/server-safety.md. This applies on vetted hosts too: vetted means the user accepts the agent working there, not that mistakes there are cheap.

Deleting or overwriting without a backup — files, directories, databases, configs, .env. Take the backup first and verify the file actually appeared; do not trust an exit code. This has silently failed before in this user's projects (delete_partner.js).
Writes to a production database — deleteMany, updateMany, DROP, TRUNCATE, schema migrations, one-off normalization scripts run with --apply. Confirm, and back up first.
Bash(rm -rf:*) and other recursive or forced deletes — irreversible; name the exact paths before running
Bash(git push --force:*), history rewrites, branch and tag deletion — confirm before running
Restarting, stopping, or redeploying a live service — confirm, and capture the current state first so there is something to compare against
Changes to system settings, permissions, network or firewall configuration — confirm before running
Bash(schtasks /delete:*) and Bash(schtasks /change:*) — scheduled-task removal or reconfiguration on this Windows host persists beyond the session; confirm before running
Bash(taskkill /f:*) — force-killing processes on this Windows host can destroy unsaved work outside the session
